title: Brake for corners
summary: Reward speed without rewarding crashes, and give the brain a way to see a bend before it arrives.

steps.title: A little reward for speed
steps.body:
Checkpoints already favor cars that get further in the time they have. A small reward for speed, paid every tick, adds a push toward driving fast.

Keep it small. At 20 m/s, `0.002 * car.speed` pays about 1.2 points per second, close to what the checkpoints pay. Make it much bigger and cars learn to floor it into the first wall, because speed alone pays more than getting round the bend.

Small extra rewards that hint at what good driving looks like are called reward shaping.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses car.speed.

hints: A reward can be a number times a sensor, with no when part.
Replace the comment with reward +0.002 * car.speed.

steps.title: See the bend coming
steps.body:
Rays see walls. They cannot see that the road turns hard 40 m ahead, and a car at 25 m/s needs about 25 m to brake.

`track.curvatureAhead(distance: 40 m)` says how sharply the road bends that far ahead. Curvature is 1 divided by the bend's radius, so a 20 m radius bend reads 0.05 per meter. Left bends are positive and right bends negative.

Add a sensor for it with the range `-0.05 1/m .. 0.05 1/m`. Now the brain can learn to brake before the bend instead of in it.

check.message: Add a sensor that reads track.curvatureAhead.

hints: You built a sensor in lesson 3. The value this time is a call with a distance.
Add sensor bendFar "Bend 40 m ahead" in -0.05 1/m .. 0.05 1/m = track.curvatureAhead(distance: 40 m).

steps.title: Do not slide
steps.body:
When a car asks for more grip than its tires have, it slides. `car.slip` goes from 0 (full grip) to 1 (a full slide). Braking and turning share the same grip, so the fast way through a bend is to brake first, then turn.

Add a small penalty for sliding. A penalty is a reward with a minus sign.

Give the limit a name with `let slipLimit = 0.3` at the top, then use it in the reward. Named numbers make a rule read like a sentence, and you can tune them in one place.

check.message: Add a penalty inside each tick that uses car.slip.

hints: A let line at the top looks like let name = value. Rewards can compare a sensor with that name.
Add let slipLimit = 0.3 at the top and reward -0.05 when car.slip > slipLimit in each tick.
